kurz: Why what matters most about the circle of competence is knowing its boundary, and how this boundary can be checked for shares and investment products.

bloecke.md:
The [[Circle of competence (Kompetenzkreis)|circle of competence]] is a statement about how far your own ability to make forecasts extends, and more than a list of industries. It covers everything about which you can say with good reason how it will stand economically in five years, and nothing beyond that. In Buffett's pointed formulation, the size of the circle does not matter, so a large circle is no proof of special abilities. What matters is knowing its boundaries precisely and not crossing them.

This changes the yardstick. What is rewarded is less knowledge itself than a correct assessment of your own knowledge. An investor who has thoroughly understood three business models and draws a clear outer boundary is in a better position than someone with thirty opinions and no boundary. The most important result of the exercise is therefore the boundary, and less so the content.

## Understanding in practice

Four questions decide whether an investment lies inside or outside the circle. The first concerns where the earnings will come from in five years, that is, whether from volume, price or cost reduction. The second concerns the capital that has to be tied up for this, and the part of it that flows back. The third clarifies who can attack the business and what the attack would cost them. The fourth asks which specific observation would refute your own thesis. If the fourth question cannot be answered, the thesis cannot be tested and is therefore merely a hope.

Two properties make handling the circle difficult. First, it is not transferable. You can adopt someone else's judgement, but not someone else's competence. This is the problem with every succession, including at Berkshire, whose quarterly report for the second quarter of 2026 already names Greg Abel as President and Chief Executive Officer. Second, the circle goes out of date. A business that was understood in 2016 may be a different one in 2026, because regulation, technology or the cost of capital have changed. The circle therefore has to be redrawn again and again.
The circle of competence describes a boundary, not a body of knowledge. Its value depends less on its content than on consistently making no decisions outside the boundary.

bloecke.titel: Familiarity and understanding as separate axes
bloecke.unter: The most expensive quadrant is the bottom right, in which an investment is familiar enough to convey a sense of security but too little understood to justify it.
bloecke.yLabel: Understanding of the business or product

felder.text: The part of the circle acquired through effort: bond mechanics, foreign markets, tax rules that you have worked out for yourself without experiencing them every day. This is where the circle grows.
The core of the circle. Only here can a deviation from market weighting be justified, and even then only to a limited extent because of cluster risk.
The too-hard pile. Whatever lies here is bought along via the broad market without an individual judgement. That way nothing is lost.
Your employer's shares, DAX companies, your own bank's product, the app on your own phone. Familiarity is easily mistaken for information.

bloecke.md:
For the bottom right quadrant, behavioural research has two terms, familiarity bias and home bias. As of 31 August 2026, the MSCI World gave the USA a weight of 72.14% and Germany less than 2.4%. A portfolio of ten German industrial shares is therefore a concentrated bet on a fringe segment of the world market and not broad diversification. The feeling of knowing the companies masks this risk.

This leads to the most common misuse of the concept. The sentence “I only buy what I understand” becomes the justification for overweighting what is familiar. But the fact that a product is used every day says nothing about the capital intensity, pricing power or competition of the business behind it.

Peter Lynch's advice to “invest in what you know” is also regularly taken as a buy signal. Lynch meant it as the starting point of research. After that, he read annual reports and spoke to the companies. For him, knowing a shop in the shopping centre was only the first step.

## No guarantee of success

Professional fund managers by definition work within their declared circle of competence, with teams of analysts, access to the companies and on a full-time basis. Nevertheless, in the ten years to 30 June 2025, 98.22% of euro-denominated active global equity funds missed their benchmark; for German equity funds, the figure was 93.68%. The rate deliberately also includes the funds that were closed or merged during the period. In the USA, over twenty years, this applied to around 63% of the equity funds that existed at the start of the period.

The result is explained by arithmetic and not by incompetence. Before costs, the average actively managed euro must earn the market return, and after costs necessarily less (Sharpe, 1991). Competence in a business and competence in beating the market after fees are therefore two different circles.

bloecke.unter: SPIVA Europe Mid-Year 2025, euro-denominated funds, including the funds closed during the period. Even in their own specialist area, only a few funds beat the market.

bloecke.md:
For private investors, the cost of crossing the boundary can be measured directly. Barber and Odean analysed 66,465 households at a US discount broker from the years 1991 to 1996. The average household achieved 16.4% a year, the market 17.9%. The most active fifth, defined by a monthly portfolio turnover of more than 8.8%, only managed 11.4%. Before costs, the frequent traders were hardly worse than the others. The gap arose almost entirely from the costs of trading.

A further study by Odean (1999) with 10,000 accounts from the years 1987 to 1993 shows that a problem of competence comes on top of the fees. The shares bought by private investors performed 3.31 percentage points worse over the following twelve months than those they sold. The swap itself therefore reduced value, even before fees and taxes. Anyone who trades a great deal is thus implicitly claiming a very large circle of competence.

bloecke.titel: Net return by trading activity, US private accounts 1991-1996
bloecke.unter: Barber/Odean (2000), 66,465 households. Before costs, all three groups were close together; the difference arises from the costs of trading and not from selection.

bloecke.md:
There is no study showing that a self-drawn circle of competence increases returns. The concept is a rule of thumb from practice and not a tested strategy. Only the costs incurred when the circle is overstepped can be measured, such as trading losses, home bias and underperformance. That is a weaker argument than it sounds.

The popular Dunning-Kruger effect is also of only limited value as evidence. Kruger and Dunning (1999) found that the weakest quarter of participants scored in the 12th percentile but rated themselves at the 62nd percentile. Later work (including Gignac/Zajenkowski and Nuhfer et al.) largely explains this pattern through regression to the mean and general overconfidence. A specific metacognitive deficit is not needed to explain it. The statement “the ignorant think they are competent” is therefore not refuted, but it is not a hard finding either. Hard feedback comes from comparing your own return after costs and taxes with a simple world index.

## The too-hard pile

In practice, a third tray is added to the “buy” and “don't buy” trays: the “too hard” tray. Everything that is rejected because no judgement can be formed, rather than because it is bad, ends up there. Examples are a biotech share before the approval decision, a bank balance sheet with an opaque trading book, or a business model whose source of earnings cannot be named in two sentences.

“Too hard” does not mean doing without investments in this area. The honest way of dealing with the area outside the circle is to buy it along at the market price instead of judging it. A broad index fund is the conscious decision not to pass judgement in thousands of individual cases. This decision not to judge has nothing to do with passivity and is the only honest stance outside the circle.

Buffett himself documented that the circle offers no guarantee even within its boundaries.

bloecke.titel: Three of Buffett's own mistakes from his shareholder letters
zeilen: Berkshire Hathaway (textiles)
approx. $100bn

A declining business was bought because it was cheap, and in 1967 the insurer National Indemnity was placed in this company instead of in the partnership. Buffett estimated the amount himself in 2015.
Dexter Shoe
approx. $5.7bn (as of 2014)
A durable competitive advantage was assumed that did not exist. The mistake was made worse by paying with Berkshire's own undervalued shares worth $433 million.
Tesco
$444m after tax
The mistake lay less in the analysis than in the hesitation. The problem in the management had been recognised, but the sale was put off. Munger calls this “thumb-sucking”.

bloecke.md:
A counterexample appears in the same letters. In 1972, See's Candies cost $25 million, with $30 million in revenue, less than $5 million in pre-tax profit and only $8 million of capital employed. By 2014, the business had generated cumulative pre-tax profits of around $1.9 billion and required only $40 million of additional capital in total to do so. The difference from Dexter Shoe lay less in diligence than in one of the four questions, namely who can attack the business and what the attack would cost them. This question could be answered in one case and not in the other.

The concentration on a few holdings is still visible today. As of the second quarter of 2026, the five positions Alphabet, American Express, Apple, Bank of America and Coca-Cola made up around 66% of Berkshire's equity portfolio. Berkshire therefore invests within a small circle, but with large amounts there.

schritte.text: The circle only grows in one direction at a time. You work your way into an industry, an asset class or a set of rules over months, not over a weekend.

The basis is the annual report, the securities prospectus, the key information document and the text of the law. A conviction based only on secondary texts does not expand your own circle; it adopts someone else's.

schritte.titel: Write it down before the decision
schritte.text: Note down the expectation, range and date. Without this record, it cannot be shown that the topic lies within the circle, because memory adjusts after the fact.
Position size depends on demonstrated understanding and not on the strength of conviction. In new areas, you start small or not at all.

bloecke.md:
## Application to product selection

For securities, the law even requires the boundary to be queried. Anyone placing orders without advice goes through the **appropriateness test** under Section 63(10) WpHG (Securities Trading Act). The institution collects information on knowledge and experience and assesses whether the instrument is appropriate. For pure order execution in non-complex financial instruments, the test does not apply at all (Section 63(11) WpHG). With investment advice, it is replaced by the **suitability test** with a written suitability statement (Section 64(3) and (4) WpHG).

However, the test relies on self-disclosure. Investors who tick the box for derivatives experience in the sign-up form in order to lift a restriction are not outwitting the broker. They are switching off the only outsider who could have marked the boundary. The forms ask the same question in institutionalised form and are only as good as the answers to them.

punkte: The source of earnings can be named in three sentences.
It has been recorded in advance which observation would refute the thesis.
The total costs from spread, ongoing charges and initial charge are known.
The tax treatment and the relevant loss pot are clear.
There is an explanation of why the other side is selling.
The argument is how well known the brand is, or your own use of the product.
The reasoning consists of the price chart and sentiment.
Risks are named but not quantified.
The key information document is available but has not been read.
The decisive argument comes from someone who earns from the sale.

bloecke.titel: Tax law in the circle of competence
bloecke.md: Knowing a product also means knowing the rules that reduce its return, and these rules change. Losses from share sales may still only be offset against gains from share sales (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG, Income Tax Act). The once-feared €20,000 limit for losses from derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte) and bad debts (Section 20(6) sentences 5 and 6 EStG, former version), on the other hand, was abolished without replacement by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz) of 2 December 2024. It no longer applies in any open cases (Section 52(28) EStG). Investors who rely on a guide from 2023 in 2026 are therefore reckoning with a rule that no longer exists.

The circle of competence is thus less a tool for selection than one for rejection. It does not produce winners, but it prevents a certain kind of failure, namely the kind in which nobody can explain afterwards what was being bet on. Its benefit cannot be measured like a return, but the consequences of breaching it can. They show up in trading costs, cluster risks and products whose construction you only read about once you have made a loss.

Only a comparison over several years, in which your own return after costs and taxes is set against a broad world index, reliably shows whether the circle runs where you think it does. Your own feeling does not provide this feedback. If the result is disappointing, that does not speak against competence. It then shows more precisely where the boundary of the circle runs.

mitnehmen: The size of the circle of competence does not matter; what is important is that its boundary is known and not crossed.
Familiarity is not competence; home bias and familiarity bias are regularly justified with the sentence “I only buy what I understand”.
Whatever is on the too-hard pile is bought along via the broad market without a judgement of your own; the pile does not mean giving up the investment.
Competence in a business and competence in beating the market after costs are two different circles; over ten years, 98.22% of euro-denominated active global equity funds missed their benchmark.

For products, the boundary runs along specific questions about the source of earnings, liability, costs, exit and taxation, which can be answered from the prospectus, the key information document and the law.

begriffe.text: Area in which someone can assess the economic development of a company or product over years on a sound basis. According to Buffett, what matters is knowing its boundary precisely, not its size.
Third tray alongside buy and reject, for cases in which no judgement is possible. These cases are not assessed individually and are instead held as part of the broad market.
Tendency to regard what is familiar as safer and easier to assess. Related to it is home bias, in which investors weight their home market more heavily than its share of the world market warrants.

Collection of information on the customer's knowledge and experience before non-advised transactions under Section 63(10) WpHG (Securities Trading Act). It is based on self-disclosure and does not apply to non-complex instruments in execution-only business.

Standardised short document for packaged investment products under the PRIIPs Regulation (EU) No. 1286/2014, with a risk indicator, costs and scenarios. It is the first source for checking whether a product lies within the circle of competence.
